# The nightly drift alarm's fifth probe: the curated slice of OpenShift's
# own suite, run against the nightly cluster through the tests binary the
# release payload ships. The list is fixed on purpose: a release that
# renames or removes a listed test fails the alarm instead of quietly
# narrowing it, and raising a verified line includes re-curating this
# list against that line's release.
#
# Curation: tests that exercise the API surface and pass green on a
# healthy nodeless control plane, so the alarm fires on drift, not on
# designed limits. Excluded, with reasons:
# - tests that require nodes, because pods must schedule and run
#   (router serving, idling, builds, LDAP identity provider, image
#   import and pull)
# - tests that require deliberately-unrun operators (the image registry
#   operator's config, the version operator's update states, the
#   operator-created api Services behind the aggregated health checks)
# - tests driven through the oc binary, which this alarm does not ship
# - tests tagged [Slow] or [Disruptive]
#
# Trimmed from the natural green selection of 96 to fit the nightly
# window: the slowest per-test costs (project watch and scoped access,
# cluster-wide quota control, serial image admission) and duplicate
# variants within a family (template instance impersonation, legacy RBAC
# proxy endpoints, role binding restrictions, JSON patch, audit rule
# rejection, pod security mapping, late lifecycle observation).
#
# Baseline: 62 tests, 5m12s wall, all green on 5.0.1 (2026-11-13),
# reproduced on a second fresh boot of the same release.
#
# The alarm strips comment and blank lines before feeding the rest to
# the runner, one test name per line, because the runner accepts
# nothing else in the file.
